1973 Pontiac LeMans Found in Neighbor's Garage, Minor Restoration Now Needed
41 photos
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics
You won’t find many of these LeMans Sport Coupes these days. That’s right, this is a 1973 LeMans Sport Coupe, and according to the current owner, it spent years locked in a garage.
The car is being described as “very unmolested,” though the paint appears to be the first obvious thing that’s been changed. The car wears a cosmetic GT treatment, but the owner is honest and says that it looks like it was repainted some years ago.
No further specifics are available at this point, but it’s still a Pontiac, and it’s still a LeMans Sport Coupe. I doubt it’ll remain available for too long, as long as the price is correct.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics Pontiac ’s big engines were struggling to remain relevant in the early ‘70s. The new regulations and the rising insurance costs pushed more and more buyers to smaller engines. The GTO suffered, and so did other models whose main point was the performance under the hood.
The LeMans continued to be a popular name in the United States, and despite General Motors still keeping some potent engines around, it was also looking beyond the muscle under the hood.
The new Luxury LeMans, whose purpose was to impress with exquisite features, was the living proof. It got a center armrest covered in Morrokdie vinyl or Bravo cloth and Morrokide, front bucket seats in Morrokide, a custom cushion steering wheel with simulated walnut inserts, wood details on the glove box door, and so many other goodies.
The LeMans Sport Coupe was supposed to retain Pontiac’s appetite for a boost of adrenaline behind the wheel without necessarily going for massive engines. “You expect sporty-looking cars from Pontiac. And we have an exciting new one for you,” Pontiac said.
That’s exactly what the LeMans Sport Coupe was all about, as it was supposed to look sporty without being sporty.
While buyers could also get the GTO package , the engine lineup started with a lazy 250 six whose purpose was to provide buyers with an efficient ride. The 350 - the most popular engine this year - could be had with two or four barrels, and so could the 400. A 455 four-barrel was offered alongside a 455 SD on the two-door LeMans and the Sport Coupe.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics This LeMans Sport Coupe is fitted with a 350ci engine paired with an automatic transmission. “It runs and drives very good,” according to the owner, but that’s all the information we’re getting at this point.
There’s one thing that intrigued me, so I recommend that buyers who are pondering making an offer contact the seller and arrange an in-person inspection. The owner says this car is mostly unmolested, so the 350 V8 engine under the hood should also be untouched. That’s not something you see every day, especially considering that the car has been sitting for several years in a garage and that it has never been rebuilt.
The seller claims some receipts dating back to the ‘80s are also available, so you should check these in person to figure out if this V8 unit has previously received any substantial work.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics Otherwise, this Pontiac looks good, and I don’t think that the rust damage is a major concern. I would still raise it on a lift to check the underside, but the seller claims that the only rust spots are on the lower body. They should be easy to deal with, though it’s probably a good idea to get closer to this car and check both the paint and these signs of rust more thoroughly.
I don’t see any bubbling behind the paint, but these are just photos posted online. The seller claims they also have videos revealing the car more thoroughly, so ask for them if you’re interested in a purchase.
The cabin also looks to be in good shape, but some repairs would still be needed, including on the seats. The driver’s seat shows its age, but dealing with the damage we see in the pics isn’t a major challenge for someone with the right experience.
The owner says the vehicle has recently been serviced, so it now has a new exhaust and tires. It sells with 3 sets of keys and a complete air conditioning system that’s already installed on the car but doesn’t work due to what seems to be a broken blower.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics As I said earlier, these cars are definitely worth a chance, especially if they are priced correctly.
The owner of this LeMans Sport Coupe believes $9,900 is just a fair expectation, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay to let people submit their offers easily. 91 people have added this car to their watchlists, so there’s a chance it’ll leave for a new garage before the listing expires in 22 days.
The car is parked in New York Mills, New York, and considering its shape, you may not need to spend additional dollars on shipping because you should be able to drive it to your shop on its wheels.
